import re
import pytest
from target import unescapeHTML, _htmlentity_transform  # type: ignore


def expected_old_unescape(s):
    """Replicate the old implementation using the original regex."""
    if s is None:
        return None
    assert isinstance(s, str)
    return re.sub(r'&([^&;]+;)', lambda m: _htmlentity_transform(m.group(1)), s)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_str,expected",
    [
        ("&", "&"),
        ("Hello <world>!", "Hello <world>!"),
        ("Mix & match "quotes"", "Mix & match \"quotes\""),
        ("No entities here", "No entities here"),
        ("&unknown;", "&unknown;"),  # unknown entity stays unchanged
    ],
)
def test_unescapeHTML_basic_cases(input_str, expected):
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected
    # also verify that the old behaviour would give the same result
    assert expected_old_unescape(input_str) == expected


def test_unescapeHTML_none():
    assert unescapeHTML(None) is None
    assert expected_old_unescape(None) is None


def test_unescapeHTML_type_assertion():
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        unescapeHTML(123)  # not a string


def test_unescapeHTML_entity_with_internal_ampersand():
    """
    Strings that contain an '&' inside what looks like an entity should NOT be altered.
    Old regex: r'&([^&;]+;)'
    New regex: r'&([^;]+;)'
    The following input would be incorrectly transformed by the new regex.
    """
    input_str = "&foo&bar; &"
    # Old behaviour: only the valid & is transformed; the malformed &foo&bar; stays as‑is
    expected = "&foo&bar; &"
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected
    # Verify that the old implementation would produce the same result
    assert expected_old_unescape(input_str) == expected


def test_unescapeHTML_multiple_mixed_entities():
    """
    Ensure that a mix of valid entities and malformed ones are handled correctly.
    """
    input_str = "Start < &bad&entity; middle & end &unknown;."
    # Only < and & should be unescaped; others remain unchanged
    expected = "Start < &bad&entity; middle & end &unknown;."
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected
    assert expected_old_unescape(input_str) == expected
